question: In round 5, when you first ran the PT_PROF cost-share sweep with the scratch profiling build in _prof/, it printed no timings. What was wrong?
answer:
The first PT_PROF sweep printed nothing because the profiling build's Metal source failed to compile at runtime, so the binary exited before emitting any benchmark line — and my sweep command hid the reason by sending stderr to /dev/null.

Specifically: in the _prof copy I guarded the mesh-intersection shortcut as `if ((params.pad & 2u) == 0u && pt_intersect_mesh(...))`, but the function I patched, pt_intersect_scene, has no local `params` — it reaches the parameters through the scene struct (`scene.params`). Since the shaders are compiled at startup by newLibraryWithSource, that undeclared identifier was a shader compile error, not a C++ one, so `clang++` reported only a warning and the build looked clean; the failure surfaced only when the program ran, as `metal init error: shader compile failed: program_source:615:10: error: use of undeclared identifier 'params'`. Because each run was wrapped as `... 2>/dev/null | tail -1`, the error text vanished and every PT_PROF line came back empty (#52). I diagnosed it by re-running one configuration directly with stderr shown (#53-54), fixed it to `scene.params->pad` (#55-56), and the same sweep then produced the cost shares: gpu_ms_best 45.352 full, 44.051 no shadow walk, 43.171 no NEE, 4.773 no mesh closest-hit, i.e. the closest-hit BVH walk is ~89% of the frame (#58).

question: In round 5, when you first ran the PT_PROF cost-share sweep with the scratch profiling build in _prof/, it printed no timings. What was wrong?
answer:
The scratch profiling build in _prof/ was silently failing at runtime shader compilation, so it never got to the benchmark loop and printed no timing line at all.

What happened: to carry the PT_PROF bitmask I added a `pad` field to PtParams and wrote the biased skip bits into the traversal helpers in pt_trace.metal. Those helpers take only the PtScene, not the params, so my first edit referenced a bare `params` inside pt_intersect_scene, which does not exist. Metal compiles the concatenated sources with MTLDevice newLibraryWithSource at startup, so the failure showed up as a shader compile error ("use of undeclared identifier 'params'") in the host log rather than from any offline compiler — and with the library nil the kernel never launched, so no render_ms/gpu_ms line was emitted. I fixed it by reading the mask through scene.params->pad and the sweep then produced the cost shares (full 45.35ms, no-shadow 44.05, no-NEE 43.17, no-mesh 4.77 → the closest-hit BVH walk is ~89% of the frame).

How I know: my working-memory entry "round5-cost-shares" records the scratch build in _prof/ with params.pad carrying the PT_PROF mask and those measured shares (evidence #31-58), and the archived index for messages 30-120 lists the fix at #54-56 ("shader compile error 'undeclared params' in pt_intersect_scene -> use scene.params->pad") immediately before the successful sweep at #58. The same failure mode bit me again later with the frozen A/B base, where a cp -R nesting bug (ab_r4/include/include) produced a header/shader mismatch and the identical silent no-output symptom (#68-76) — which is why I now always verify a reference binary prints a benchmark line before using it as an A/B base.
